meta.title: Dhaniverse contracts: food market, money, quests and names
meta.status: Built in contracts/. CI checks that every public function, event and error of ours has a plain-English line here.
meta.foundation: ⛓️ Standing on Ethereum Sepolia (Circle USDC, Uniswap v4, ENSv2); anvil locally
meta.roofOne: The Rust server runs the game and signs tickets and vouchers; its chain crate sends transactions and indexes events. Each key it holds can press only certain functions.
meta.fuseNote: FoodToken and FoodHook have no off switch. Everywhere else, replacing a key (signer, keeper) or taking a role away is the off switch, and every read keeps working.
meta.phasesHint: Built bottom to top, one phase at a time.

summary: USDC is the only money. Players buy food (energy) with USDC through MealCounter; every meal is a real Uniswap v4 swap in the FOOD/USDC pool, whose hook keeps the price in a band. Food revenue reaches Treasury, which feeds HousePool (fixed rewards, surprises, rescue meals, each capped at 4% a day). Sponsors fund campaigns in CampaignEscrow (10% fee, the 25% rule, daily caps, advances, refunds); FloatManager holds their USDC and earns (simulated, on testnet) yield for the house pool. The Spice Run sends players through Uniswap's Universal Router to SpiceMerchant; LuckyLedger runs the free weekly draw; ENSv2 names everyone under tallyport.eth.
needFromYou: Fund the Sepolia deployer with Circle test USDC (faucet.circle.com) and Sepolia ETH, then run script/Deploy.s.sol.
Run the ENS setup (script/names/CityNames.s.sol) to register tallyport.eth and name the contracts.
Hand every contract's admin role to a multisig after the demo (transferOwnership + acceptOwnership).

promises.title: The game never waits for the chain
promises.text: Players never sign anything or pay gas. Walking, working and eating never touch a chain. Bank actions confirm in about a second behind an animation, and names catch up in the background.

promises.title: Every error names itself
promises.text: No vague failures. Each refusal says which contract, what went wrong, and the numbers that caused it. Our tool, dhv why, adds the plain-English meaning and the exact file and line.

promises.title: If a chain breaks, the city doesn't
promises.text: If Arc or Sepolia is slow, or a key is switched off, the game keeps running: menus keep the last prices, bank actions wait in order, and names show from our database.

promises.title: Fixable without losing anything
promises.text: A broken contract is replaced and its ENS name repointed, and the server follows the name. Every fix starts as a failing test and runs on a test world first.

promises.title: Every function in plain words
promises.text: Every function on every contract is listed here: who presses it, when, and what happens. Once code exists, CI fails if a public function has no plain-English line in this spec.

workLoop.title: Brief
workLoop.text: Before any code: a short page with this phase's contracts, functions and decisions. You say go, or change it.

workLoop.title: Build
workLoop.text: I write the code and its tests. Money rules get their tests first.

workLoop.title: Prove
workLoop.text: Every test green, the numbers below hit exactly, and Arc Studio gives a second opinion.

workLoop.title: Show
workLoop.text: A phase report: what was built, what each function does, test results, anything that changed from this map, and one command to run it yourself.

workLoop.title: You review
workLoop.text: Then it merges and the next phase starts.

flows.title: Buying a thali
flows.lede: Every meal is a real swap and burn.

steps.text: Sam buys a thali at the Common Table.
Quotes 6 FOOD × live price + 2% and signs a MealTicket.
Sam's wallet calls MealCounter.buyMeal: FoodRouter buys 6 FOOD (burned); any shortfall from the ration reserve at band-high; the rest refunded.
The indexer sees MealEaten and credits +70 energy.
Sam is short: the server signs an AdvanceVoucher; CampaignEscrow advances $0.50.
Sam's wallet swaps USDC→MANGO through the Universal Router (V4_SWAP).
SpiceMerchant.deliver forwards MANGO to the sponsor.
The indexer sees the Swap and Delivered; the server signs a CampaignClaim; escrow repays the advance first and pays the rest.

dhv why names the contract, the error, the numbers and the line.
Write a test that fails because of the bug. Now the bug can never quietly come back.
Change the code until that test and every other test pass.

fixSteps.t: Try it on a test world first
fixSteps.d: Deploy the fix to a fresh test world and replay the last days of trades.

Deploy the fixed contract and point its ENS name at it (bank.dhaniverse.eth or market.dhaniverse.eth); the server follows the name. FoodRouter swaps without touching the pool or its history. A new CityBank is rebuilt from the old one's public records: the server re-deposits each balance and reopens each loan with what's left to pay. A FoodHook bug means a new hook and pool; the server carries the price history over.

fixSteps.t: Switch back on and write it down
fixSteps.d: Give the keys their roles back. The changelog says what broke and why, and you approve it.

decisions.pick: USDC only (founder rule). No coins, no play money.
decisions.why: One currency keeps the economy honest and legible.

decisions.pick: The player's own wallet calls MealCounter with a server-signed ticket.
decisions.why: No bots outside the game, no hoarding, a real swap per meal.

decisions.q: Does the router cap what a meal costs?
decisions.pick: Yes: buyFood takes maxUsdc and refuses with FoodRouter__TooDear.
decisions.why: Token-agnostic: Circle USDC's string reverts can't be mapped to a clean error otherwise.

decisions.q: How does a player own their shop sign?
decisions.pick: Each player's name gets its own Permissioned Resolver; the player's wallet holds the text role for description and avatar on it.
decisions.why: ENSv2 roles are per resolver and per key, not per name.
decisions.alt: A shared players' resolver (any player could edit any sign).

decisions.pick: Uniswap's own Sepolia bytecode placed at the Sepolia addresses (script/anvil).
decisions.why: The server uses one set of addresses and the real Universal Router everywhere.
decisions.alt: v4 test routers (different code path) or forking Sepolia (needs network).

decisions.why: Same as Uniswap v4; via-IR bugs avoided.

rules.d: A contract does one thing. A second job gets a second contract.
Contracts are nouns (FoodRouter), functions are verbs (buyFood), events are past tense (FoodBought), errors name the contract and the problem (FoodRouter__RefUsed).
Not just 'too much', but how much and what the limit was.
Each state change emits an event, so the server's indexer can replay history into the world log.
1,000,000 base units = 1 USDC. FOOD also has 6 decimals. Prices are USDC base units per whole FOOD.
Checks first, then update the records, and only then move money (checks-effects-interactions).
Every read function works even when every key is switched off.

rules.t: Every action has a ref, and a ref works once
rules.d: That's how a retry can never pay, charge or buy twice.

rules.t: Short, one-way links between our contracts
rules.d: Each link is a small interface in src/money/Links.sol and listed under talksTo. Money only ever moves in the direction the spec says.
The server finds our contracts and players by ENS name. The only fixed entry point is ENS's own, which the alloy library already knows.

rules.t: Budgets are fixed at the day's first payout
rules.d: HousePool's 4% and each campaign's daily cap are snapshotted on the first payout of a UTC day, so a day can never spend more than its budget.
Every bug becomes a test before it's fixed.

rules.t: The spec and the code can't drift
rules.d: CI fails if a public function has no plain-English line here.
Every number is a named constant with its unit in the name.
